iterations.summary: Inserted a fully registered instruction-request slice between the frontend and instruction HXI master. The slice breaks the branch-miss, queue-credit and fetch-request control cone before HXI arbitration and external BRAM controls while retaining one accepted request per cycle.

timing.worst_path: DCache data-bank BRAM through load-completion operand bypass and the address-generation adder to exec_mem_addr_q

verification: WSL final ISA gate PASS: 76/76 RV32UI/RV32MI/RV32UM/RV32UF
RT-Thread ps/help follow-up commands and shell prompt recovery PASS
Manual bitstream export from final post-route physopt checkpoint PASS
Physical board validation PASS at 150 MHz; CoreMark 10000 measured approximately 26.3 seconds

board_safety.request_slice_policy: Requests already accepted by the frontend are never flushed in the slice; stale responses return normally and are discarded by the frontend epoch mechanism. Flushing an accepted request would strand its pending metadata and can cause the historical no-response or repeated-trap board failure.
board_safety.clock_contract: MMCM, RTL/board metadata, SoC and timer frequency, UART cycles per bit, CoreMark timebase and embedded firmware all remain one generated 150 MHz set.
board_safety.uart_simulation_fix: The Verilator launcher now applies the generated UART cycles-per-bit contract to every simulation, including receive-less smoke tests.
board_safety.branch_prediction: No branch predictor table, policy, history or update logic was changed.
board_safety.physical_board_status: PASS: v3.1 was physically validated at 150 MHz; user-reported CoreMark 10000 runtime is approximately 26.3 seconds.

decision.reason: It enters the accepted timing envelope with a 99.46 percent TNS reduction while retaining the CoreMark cycle limit. Further pipelining of the new DCache-to-AGU worst path would directly risk the remaining 48168-cycle margin and broaden the board-validation surface.
